title: Compact ingest protocol and atomic re-enqueue for safe idempotent retries
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal:
Streamline the ingest + delivery executor to (1) reduce head-of-line blocking under tenant hotspots, (2) provide an atomic re-enqueue path that preserves idempotency metadata, and (3) eliminate blocking Redis/Kafka client calls in critical hot paths. This ticket consolidates work across the ingress, prefetch, and retry layers into a compact protocol with clearer handoffs and observability.

Background:
Over time the ingest pipeline accumulated incremental fixes: synchronous Redis calls in the worker lease path, ad-hoc re-enqueue logic that drops idempotency headers, and duplicated backpressure heuristics across Redis/Kafka consumers. These have caused periodic tenant hotspots that inflate tail latency and increase duplicate deliveries during retries.

Success criteria:
- Per-tenant inflight limit enforced without global head-of-line blocking (95th percentile per-tenant latency reduced by 20% on load tests).
- Re-enqueue is atomic w.r.t. idempotency metadata: dedup keys, original request cursor, and retry count preserved across restarts.
- No blocking calls on the hot path (migrate synchronous Redis client APIs to async/nonblocking client).
- End-to-end integration tests cover at-least-once and dedup paths, simulated partition loss, and drain.
- Canary rollout plan and metrics to safely ramp to 100%.

Design summary:
1) Protocol compactness: replace multi-stage handoff (ingest -> prefetch -> executor -> retry) with a two-message contract per work unit: CLAIM (lease + minimal metadata) and ACK/REQUEUE (terminal info). CLAIM contains a compact descriptor and an idempotency token; ACK/REQUEUE carries outcome and optionally a re-enqueue policy.

2) Atomic re-enqueue: on transient failures, workers will issue a single atomic REQUEUE operation that appends the original descriptor to the target stream/queue with preserved metadata and increments RetryCounter via a single Redis Lua script when using Redis-backed queues, or via a transactional producer with headers when using Kafka. The goal is to avoid windows where the message is visible without its dedup token.

3) Tenant-aware inflight controller: introduce a token-bucket style per-tenant controller (soft and hard caps). The controller lives in-process with optional shared state for observability; it accepts CLAIMs only while tokens are available, otherwise returns a polite backpressure response that the ingress can use to delay or route to lower-cost variants.

4) Async client upgrade: adopt the native async Redis client (neo-redis-async v2.1) and migrate internal helpers to non-blocking APIs. Remove blocking futures from the hot path. For Kafka, use the async producer with idempotent headers and await broker ACKs only in the retry coordinator, not on the main exec path.

5) Observability & metrics: emit per-tenant inflight, claim wait time, atomic-requeue failures, dedup-miss rate, and partition-rebalance impact. Add tracing spans for claim->process->ack latency.

Migration & rollout:
- Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + integration harness (local redis/kafka) and synthetic tenant load (est: 1 week).
- Phase 1 (staging canary): deploy to staging cluster, run 24h soak with top-10 tenants replay (est: 3 days).
- Phase 2 (production canary): enable on 5% of traffic using routing policy and observability gates; rollback on increased duplicates or tail latency (est: 3 days).
- Phase 3: ramp to 100% with gradual increases and SLO checks.

Testing plan:
- New harness that replays recorded production traces with injectible faults (partition loss, process kill).
- Property-based tests for the Lua atomic requeue script verifying dedup token transfer invariant.
- Chaos tests for lease epoch rebalancing and drain semantics.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Centralized vs in-process per-tenant controller: chosen in-process with optional shared telemetry to avoid a central coordination bottleneck. We may revisit if memory pressure is high for many tenants.
- Redis Lua vs Kafka transactional producer for atomic re-enqueue: implement both adapters. Redis Lua will be the short-term path because it is available in existing tenants; Kafka transactional path will be an opt-in for high-throughput tenants.
- Retry counting strategy: store RetryCounter as a compact integer in metadata (avoid unbounded headers). Will require schema migration for older messages.

Non-goals:
- Addressing unrelated consumer-side prioritization algorithms (separate ticket).
- Full client library rewrite beyond the async migrations required for the hot path.
